cases.exposure_context_quote: A 40-year-old Sri Lankan man presented to the hospital five hours after deliberate ingestion of approximately 50 mL of profenofos (500 g/L emulsifiable concentrate), an organophosphate pesticide.
cases.agent: profenofos (500 g/L emulsifiable concentrate), approximately 50 mL
cases.agent_quote: deliberate ingestion of approximately 50 mL of profenofos (500 g/L emulsifiable concentrate)

symptoms.finding: no peripheral cholinergic features at admission
symptoms.quote: There were no muscarinic or nicotinic features of cholinergic excess such as hyper-salivation, lacrimation, diarrhoea, fasciculations, or bradycardia.

symptoms.finding: generalized tonic–clonic seizures (status epilepticus) at 36 h post-ingestion, refractory to midazolam boluses and levetiracetam
symptoms.quote: At 36 h post-ingestion, the patient developed generalized tonic–clonic seizures that persisted for over 15 min and were refractory to two boluses of intravenous midazolam (5 mg each).

labs.name: serum lactate (venous blood gas)
labs.value: 5.3 mmol/L (< 2 mmol/L), normalised spontaneously within six hours
labs.quote: Initial venous blood gas analysis was within normal limits, except for a raised serum lactate of 5.3 mmol/L (< 2 mmol/L), which normalised spontaneously within six hours.

labs.name: urine and serum toxicology screens
labs.value: negative for benzodiazepines, opioids, and psychostimulants
labs.quote: Urine and serum toxicology screens were negative for benzodiazepines, opioids, and psychostimulants.

labs.name: hematology, electrolytes, liver and renal biochemistry
labs.value: within normal limits throughout hospital stay
labs.quote: Haematological indices, serum electrolytes, and liver and renal biochemistry remained within normal limits throughout the hospital stay.

treatment.name: IV midazolam boluses (5 mg each, two) then continuous infusion 5 mg/hour; IV levetiracetam 2 g; neuromuscular paralysis with atracurium and endotracheal intubation
treatment.quote: Intravenous levetiracetam (2 g) was administered, followed by neuromuscular paralysis with atracurium and endotracheal intubation. A continuous intravenous midazolam infusion was commenced at 5 mg/hour.

treatment.name: IV atropine 3.6 mg empirically, then continuous infusion 0.6 mg/hour
treatment.quote: intravenous atropine (3.6 mg) was administered empirically, followed by a continuous infusion at 0.6 mg/hour.

cases.outcome: survived; full neurological recovery, extubated 72 h after ingestion, asymptomatic at six-month follow-up
cases.outcome_quote: The patient made a full neurological recovery and was successfully extubated 72 h after ingestion. The patient remained asymptomatic in a six month follow up.
cases.notes: No atropine, activated charcoal, or oxime at presentation; RBC AChE activity not measured.
